tagline: Global industrial technology company designing and deploying advanced technologies to empower everyday heroes who build, serve and protect communities around the world
hero_kpi_rationale: The defense segment represents a significant and stable portion of revenues (20% in 2025), supported by multi-year contracts with the U.S. government, making it a structural pillar of the growth trajectory despite the absence of a pure AI technology wave.

kpis.name: Defense Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total sales to the U.S. government, primarily in the military vehicles domain.
kpis.description: The company relies on approximately 20% of sales to the U.S. government, mostly through multi-year contracts in the defense segment, providing strong financial visibility.
kpis.signal: Revenue stability from long-term government contracts.

kpis.name: Access Segment Sales
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total revenues generated from manufacturing lifting and material handling equipment under the JLG and SkyTrak brands.
kpis.description: The Access segment is the largest revenue contributor with 43% of sales in 2025, driven by JLG and SkyTrak, active in construction and industrial markets.
kpis.signal: Main segment with 43% of sales, but exposed to economic cycles.

kpis.name: Vocational Segment Sales
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total revenues from fire trucks, waste management vehicles, and airport equipment.
kpis.description: The Vocational segment covers emergency, waste, and airport vehicle markets, representing 36% of total sales.
kpis.signal: Second-largest segment by size, diversified but sensitive to municipal budgets.

kpis.name: Transport Segment Sales
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total revenues related to delivery vehicles and specialized transport equipment.
kpis.description: The Transport segment represents 20% of sales, including delivery vehicles and specialized equipment.

kpis.name: Access Op Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating margin of the Access segment (lifting equipment), reflecting pressure from discounts and under-absorption of fixed costs.
kpis.description: The Access segment's operating margin declined by 440 bps to 11.2% in 2025, penalized by high commercial discounts (+190 bps) and under-absorption of fixed costs due to lower production volumes.

kpis.name: Vocational Op Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating margin of the Vocational segment (specialty trucks), benefiting from price improvements and higher production rates.
kpis.description: The Vocational operating margin improved by 270 bps to 14.7%, driven by pricing gains (+300 bps gross margin), partially offset by rising material and labor costs.

kpis.name: OSK Op Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from operating activities, the group's primary source of financing.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow surged to $783.4M in 2025 vs $550.1M in 2024, driven by significantly lower tax payments (-$238.6M) and reduced outflows related to the NGDV program.

kpis.name: Debt/Capitalization
kpis.explanation: Ratio measuring debt weight in total capital structure (debt + equity), a financial leverage indicator.
kpis.description: The debt/capitalization ratio stood at 19.5% as of December 31, 2025, slightly up from 18.8% in 2024, remaining within the group's target range and consistent with investment grade ratings (BBB/Baa3).

kpis.name: Inventory Turns
kpis.explanation: Number of times inventory is turned over during the year (annualized COGS / average inventory over 5 quarters), an operational efficiency indicator.
kpis.description: Consolidated inventory turns declined from 3.9x to 3.6x in 2025, primarily due to higher inventory levels in the Transport and Vocational segments linked to ramping production rates.

kpis.name: DPS
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.57 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Cap Return
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.13B in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 20.2% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Defense Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total sales to the U.S. government, primarily in the military vehicles domain.
kpis.description: The company relies on approximately 20% of sales to the U.S. government, mostly through multi-year contracts in the defense segment, providing strong financial visibility.
kpis.signal: Revenue stability from long-term government contracts.

risks.title: USPS NGDV Contract Risks
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, with strong language ("impairment", "lower revenues", "higher costs"). The $135M deficit on deferred costs and production delays indicate an existential risk. The Capital category is highly weighted here.

risks.title: Trade Tensions and Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: The document cites rising tariff-related costs increasing from $35M in 2025 to $200M in 2026. The language emphasizes uncertainty and direct impact on supply chain and costs. The Geopolitical category is heavily impacted.

risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeated and detailed, with mention of impact on profitability of ongoing orders. The language is concerned but mitigated by ongoing mitigation efforts. The Credit category is moderately weighted.

risks.title: Supplier Dependence and Supply Disruptions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is frequently mentioned, with concrete consequences (high costs, delays). The language is alarming but not critical. The Industrial category carries major operational impact.

risks.title: Underperforming Capacity Expansion
risks.score_rationale: The risk is prominently positioned in the document, with threats to timelines, costs, and efficiency. The language is cautious but serious. The Capital category reinforces severity.

risks.title: Increased Competition in Public Markets
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly tied to federal laws (WSARA, CICA) and potential loss of DoD contracts. The language is formal but concerned. The Competition category is significant.

risks.title: Skilled Labor Shortages
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned secondarily, without precise figures. The language is moderate. The Industrial category, but with lesser impact than others.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence was found in the provided text.
